title: The Lady Be Good tenor duet with Ted McRae
summary: Cobb and Ted McRae secretly rehearse a Lady Be Good duet in a Philadelphia theater break, Hampton keeps it, and Lucky Thompson, Herbie Fields and Johnny Griffin later play it.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: (Inaudible) about when does Johnny Griffin come in?
Johnny came in the band in '45.
Well, weren't you going to (inaudible) with anybody else (inaudible)?
Oh, you were? It would be duetting with (inaudible) --
Well, I had Elef Simon out of Houston who was duetting with me. I had Lucky Thompson, and I had MacRae. I'm trying to think of MacRae's first --

Ted MacRae. All right, let me tell you what happened. We were in Fay's Theater in Philadelphia. Remember, I told you about the Joe Thomas situation and his marriage and all this? But this was on another occasion, and my wife had to go and represent me. But Ted and I stayed in the theater. We have a long break between the -- we do one show and then we come back for a 7:30 show that night. We've got two and a half to three hours.

So I told Ted -- we're playing Lady Be Good for the number. I said, Ted, I've got a vision or an idea or something that you feel like you want to stay here and work. We can go out and get something and bring back and eat and stay here, and we'll surprise everybody. He said, good, I'm for that.

So I gave him this pattern that I had on Lady Be Good. And we rehearsed it. Nobody knew it but just the two of us. And we got it down pat. And we went over and over it, just how we were going to do it, what courses, this and that. So Hamp is a critical son of a gun. You may know. When we come back with, did the opening number, instead of down by myself, Ted and I come together. And Hamp didn't know what the heck was happening. He said, what is this? But he could shoot them bow dollar eyes at you.

But when we got through with it, we broke the house out. And he said, sa-a-sa-sa-sa-a, keep that in. And we kept it in. And it -- when Ted left the band, Lucky Thompson came in behind him. Lucky did it. Herbie Field come in behind him. He did it. And right on -- when Johnny Griffin come in, we fought on, and he's a little fizen, and I'm big 200 -- (inaudible). See how big I am? And Johnny's a little guy, and I'm stomping my feet at him, and he's little, like a little fizser, but he's blowing. Cracked it up. But we kept that same pattern for two years, traveling in the theater.
Hamp didn't want to get rid of us.
Well, did you -- now, what about Flying Home? What did you do with it?
This wasn't Flying Home. This was Lady Be Good, the opening tune of the show.
